entry.hook: The Sword of Immortal Slaying (诛仙剑) is a Primordial Slaughter Treasure that does not merely cut flesh but severs the very root of existence from the web of cause and effect. To wield it is to borrow the Dao’s most forbidden authority—the power to erase a being from the fabric of the cosmos. Every swing writes an irreversible scar on the wielder’s soul, and three such scars turn the master into a mindless slaughter puppet. This is not a weapon. It is a contract signed in blood and signed again at the cost of the self.

body.body_1:
诛仙剑 Sword of Immortal Slaying  
器属类型：先天杀伐至宝 Primordial Slaughter Treasure  
Artifact Tier: Zao Hua Xiong Qi (Creation-Forged Ominous Armament)  
Current Holder: Historically wielded by Tongtian Jiaozhu (通天教主); fate after the Investiture War is ambiguous in the tradition  
Current Status: The sword’s present location is unknown; some accounts suggest it was sealed by the Dao ancestors after the battle of the Immortal Slaying Formation
body.body_2: The Sword of Immortal Slaying is classified as a Zao Hua Xiong Qi, the highest and most dangerous tier of artifact. Its core power is not ordinary severance but the invocation of the purest “slaughter principle” (杀机) that operates at the level of causality. When the sword is drawn, it severs the target’s connection to cosmic law, karmic ties, and even their place in recorded memory. No magical defense can block this erasure, as the attack bypasses all intermediate phenomena. The wielder must possess at least the cultivation base of a Da Luo Jin Xian (大罗金仙) to withstand the sword’s ambient killing intent; anyone below that rank will have their soul shredded on contact. The sword’s range is limited only by the user’s ability to lock onto the target’s causal thread—in theory, it can strike across realms once the connection is established.
body.body_3: The Sword of Immortal Slaying was not forged in any mundane furnace. It is a primordial entity, born from the concentrated slaughter principle that crystallized during the cosmic upheavals of the Honghuang Era. No material was “mined” in the conventional sense, because the sword is itself a fragment of the Dao’s own destructive logic made tangible. Some sources within the Fengshen Yanyi tradition imply that its substance is derived from the residual killing energy left after the Primordial Gods’ wars—an incorporeal harvest that required no excavation but still scarred the nascent universe at a conceptual level. The sword’s existence alone perpetuates a subtle imbalance in the cosmic yin-yang equilibrium, much like a permanent wound in the order of things.
body.body_4: The sword contains an artifact spirit (Qi Ling) that is the sealed soul of an ancient primordial beast—a being of untold ferocity from the age before the Great Disconnection. During the sword’s shaping, this beast’s soul was captured at the moment of agony and forced into the sword’s core matrix as its animating intelligence. It is not a willing servant. It exists in a state of perpetual rage and hunger, and it can only be kept docile by regular offerings of the wielder’s own blood and spiritual essence. If the feedings are neglected, the beast-soul will overpower the artifact’s binding runes and devour the wielder from the inside. The Qi Ling has no desire for communication or partnership—it wants only to consume and to be released from its eternal prison, and it will seize any opportunity to break free.
body.body_5: Master recognition (Ren Zhu) for the Sword of Immortal Slaying is a near-suicidal undertaking. The would-be wielder must open their soul-sea to the sword and allow the killing intent to flood their being. If they survive, the sword then demands a blood pact: the wielder must periodically feed it their own lifeblood, and each activation of the sword carves an “Apocalyptic Slaughter Mark” (灭世杀痕) into the wielder’s soul. These marks are irreversible. After three such marks accumulate, the wielder’s consciousness is overwritten, and they become a mindless, indiscriminate slaughter puppet, driven only by the sword’s own will. The sword is thus a parasite that tolerates its host only as long as the host remains strong and useful. The moment the wielder is gravely wounded or their cultivation falters, the beast-soul will attempt to consume them entirely. No historical record shows a wielder surviving three activations and retaining their sanity.
body.body_6: Only one stable wielder is recorded in canonical texts: Tongtian Jiaozhu (通天教主), the founder of the Jie Sect (截教) during the Shang dynasty. He possessed the sword as part of the Four Swords of Immortal Slaying (诛仙四剑) and deployed it in the fateful battle of the Immortal Slaying Formation against the allied forces of the Chan Sect and Western Buddhism. He did not die from the sword’s backlash, but he was ultimately defeated and his treasures confiscated by the Dao ancestors. Some later legends claim that the sword briefly passed into the hands of a fallen disciple who attempted to use it for revenge—a story that always ends with that disciple being consumed by the beast-soul within hours. The sword has no record of a wielder who died of old age.
body.body_7: The sword’s most famous deployment occurred during the Investiture War, when Tongtian Jiaozhu activated the full Immortal Slaying Formation. Supported by the other three swords and the formation diagram, the sword’s power was magnified to a level that threatened to annihilate the entire army of gods and immortals besieging the Jie Sect. The formation drew all spiritual energy from a radius of ten thousand li (approximately 5,000 km), turning fertile lands into barren wastes and causing millions of mortal deaths through the collapse of natural cycles. After this single use, the sword reportedly entered a dormant state for several years, during which the beast-soul’s demands for blood increased tenfold. The formation diagram itself required the sacrificial offering of four Da Luo Jin Xian-level true spirits to stabilize its power alignment; without that sacrifice, the sword’s slaughter principle would have turned back on the formation’s master.
body.body_8: The Sword of Immortal Slaying is the chief of the Four Swords of Immortal Slaying (诛仙四剑), the other three being the Sword of Immortal Execution (戮仙剑), Sword of Immortal Extermination (陷仙剑), and Sword of Immortal Annihilation (绝仙剑). These four swords are not merely related; they are designed to work together as a single weapon system when placed on the Immortal Slaying Formation Diagram (诛仙阵图). The diagram binds their slaughter principles into a closed, self-reinforcing loop that magnifies each sword’s power by several orders of magnitude. No independent weapon is known to specifically counter the Sword of Immortal Slaying, though the combined power of four Da Luo Jin Xian—each commanding a different celestial principle—was said to be able to disrupt the formation’s coherence. The sword is not derived from any higher-tier weapon; it is a primordial creation in its own right.
body.body_9: After the defeat of Tongtian Jiaozhu in the Investiture War, the Sword of Immortal Slaying was confiscated by the celestial authorities—variously described as the Dao Ancestors (道祖) or the supreme will of Heaven. The Fengshen Yanyi states that the sword was sealed away to prevent its slaughter principle from contaminating the newly stabilized cosmic order. Its exact resting place is not disclosed in any surviving text. Some later Daoist apocrypha claim that the sword was cast into the primordial chaos beyond the Thirty-Three Heavens, while others insist it was broken and its fragments scattered across the void. In the mainstream tradition, the sword is simply considered “no longer accessible” —a treasure too dangerous for any age.
body.body_11: The Sword of Immortal Slaying is inextricably linked to its master Tongtian Jiaozhu (通天教主), the founder of the Jie Sect, and to the Four Swords of Immortal Slaying set, which includes the Sword of Immortal Execution, the Sword of Immortal Extermination, and the Sword of Immortal Annihilation. These four swords together constitute the core armament of the Immortal Slaying Formation (诛仙阵图), a war-array that requires the sacrifice of four Da Luo Jin Xian-level true spirits to stabilize. The sword’s legend is primarily preserved through the Ming dynasty novel Fengshen Yanyi (Investiture of the Gods), which records its most famous deployment during the war between the Shang and Zhou dynasties, though its in-universe origins go back to the Honghuang Era and the crystallization of primordial slaughter principle. Readers exploring the sword should also refer to the entries on the Great Furnace (Hong Lu) and Living Soul Sacrifice (Sheng Hun Ji Ding), as the sword’s creation and operation embody the cruel logic of artifact refinement described in the Artifact Volume.

guide.guide_1: You know, there aren’t many weapons I’d describe as having a “soul-eating contract written in cosmic law” built right into the blade. But the Sword of Immortal Slaying—in Chinese, this thing is called Zhuxian Jian, and the name means exactly what it says—is one of them. Imagine a sword that doesn’t just cut through armor or magic, but actually reaches into the fabric of reality and snips out the thread that holds a being together. That’s its basic function. And then imagine that every time you swing it, it carves a permanent scar into your soul, and if you swing it three times, you stop being yourself and become a living extension of the sword’s own hunger. That’s not a movie villain’s weapon. That’s a real object from one of China’s most famous myth cycles. And the tradition insists: this thing existed.
guide.guide_2: If you’ve ever dipped into Chinese mythology—the Investiture of the Gods or the later xianxia adaptations—you’ve probably heard of the Sword of Immortal Slaying. It’s the headliner sword of the Jie Sect, the one that Tongtian Jiaozhu pulled out when things got really bad. In the stories, it’s always described as unstoppable, able to kill immortals, capable of bringing down even the most powerful beings. But what those stories often skip is the fine print: the blade is haunted by a trapped primordial beast soul that has to be fed the wielder’s own blood. And the wielder slowly loses their mind. The reason it’s so terrifying isn’t just the power—it’s the price tag you can never stop paying. Let’s walk through what it’s really like to own a weapon like this.
guide.guide_3: Let’s start with how this sword came to exist. And I want to be clear: the Sword of Immortal Slaying wasn’t forged in a furnace by a smith. It’s a primordial treasure—part of the generation of artifacts that crystallized during the Honghuang Era, when the universe was still settling into its laws. Think of it as a piece of the Dao’s own destructiveness that solidified into a physical form. There was no mining, no melting, no hammering; the sword is more like a thunderstorm that decided to hold still. But that doesn’t mean it came free. Its existence carved a conceptual wound into the cosmos, a permanent imbalance in the yin-yang equilibrium. And when the sword is activated in the full Immortal Slaying Formation, it drains all spiritual energy for ten thousand li around it. Those are not mythical flourishes—those are the costs that the Fengshen Yanyi records in black ink. The sword’s very presence is the price.
guide.guide_4: Now, let’s talk about the soul inside the blade. This is the part that keeps me awake sometimes. The Sword of Immortal Slaying contains an artifact spirit—a Qi Ling. And in this case, the Qi Ling is the bound soul of an ancient primordial beast. We don’t know its exact species or name, only that it was a being of immense power from the early age of the universe, and that its soul was captured at the moment of its death and forcibly sealed into the sword as the core animating force. This soul is not a friendly guide. It does not offer advice. It does not like you. It wants to be free, and failing that, it wants to devour anything alive. The only way to keep it quiet is to feed it your own lifeblood on a regular schedule. If you stop, the beast-soul will push past the binding runes and eat you alive. So the sword is effectively a perpetual-hunger machine disguised as a weapon. And that hunger never sleeps.
guide.guide_5: The master-recognition ritual for the Sword of Immortal Slaying is not for the faint-hearted. You don’t just cut your palm and say “I claim you.” You have to consciously open your soul-sea to the blade and let its full killing intent wash through your being. If you can survive that—and most people can’t—then the sword condescends to feed on your blood. And here’s the real horror: every time you use the sword in combat, it carves an “Apocalyptic Slaughter Mark” into your soul. These marks are permanent. After three such marks, your consciousness gets overwritten by the sword’s own will, and you become a mindless puppet that exists only to swing the blade. This is not revenge from the sword—it’s just the thermodynamic reality of wielding a piece of cosmic destruction. You trade your soul for its power. And you don’t get to keep the soul.
guide.guide_6: When it comes to people who have actually wielded this sword, the historical record is short and brutal. The only stable wielder recorded across all the texts is Tongtian Jiaozhu, the founder of the Jie Sect. He used it during the Investiture War, when his sect was surrounded by enemies from the Chan Sect and Western Buddhism. He set up the full Immortal Slaying Formation, and for a while, the sword did exactly what it was supposed to do: it nearly erased the opposing army from existence. But Tongtian Jiaozhu didn't die from the sword—he was defeated and his treasures taken away. The tradition is silent on how many Slaughter Marks he accumulated, but he was a being of extraordinary cultivation, possibly able to withstand more than the normal limit. Some lesser figures have tried to claim the sword after the war, and every single one of them either went mad or was consumed within days. There is no happy ending story for anyone else.
guide.guide_7: So here’s the deeper question: why would a universe bother to create a weapon like this? It’s not because the gods were sadistic. It’s because, in the cosmology of this volume, power is never free. The Dao doesn’t let you borrow cosmic authority without paying back something real. The Sword of Immortal Slaying is the most extreme expression of that logic—its existence is a permanent debt that someone has to keep repaying with soul and blood. And the tradition is honest about it: you cannot borrow annihilation and walk away unchanged. This principle runs through the entire Artifact Volume. Every shiing artifact, every legendary blade, every furnace-forged treasure—there’s a cost embedded in it, and the cost is always human in the end. The Sword of Immortal Slaying just makes the truth impossible to ignore. If you pick it up, you are signing a contract with cosmic slaughter. And the contract has no clause for your survival.

seo.meta_description: The Sword of Immortal Slaying (诛仙剑) is a primordial slaughter treasure that severs existence itself from the fabric of causality. Wielding it demands blood sacrifice, feeds a trapped beast soul, and carves irreversible marks on the wielder's soul. Discover the cold cost behind one of China's most legendary divine armaments.
seo.og_title: Sword of Immortal Slaying (诛仙剑) — Primordial Slaughter Treasure
seo.og_description: The Sword of Immortal Slaying is not a simple weapon; it is a prison for a primordial beast soul and a soul-devouring contract. Each swing threatens to turn the master into a mindless slaughter puppet. Explore the brutal truth of this Zao Hua Xiong Qi from the Fengshen Yanyi tradition.
seo.twitter_title: Sword of Immortal Slaying — The Blade That Eats Souls
seo.twitter_description: The legendary Sword of Immortal Slaying cuts through cause and effect, but its cost is the wielder's sanity and lifeblood. Learn why this primordial treasure is one of the most feared artifacts in Chinese mythology.

lore_entries.description: The founder of the Jie Sect during the Shang dynasty. He was the only recorded stable wielder of the Sword of Immortal Slaying and deployed it during the Investiture War.

A war-array that binds the four swords of immortal slaying into a closed, self-reinforcing loop. It requires the sacrificial offering of four Da Luo Jin Xian-level true spirits to stabilize; otherwise the slaughter principle turns on the formation's master.

A permanent, irreversible scar etched into the wielder's soul each time the sword is fully activated. Three such marks overwrite the wielder's consciousness and turn them into a mindless slaughter puppet.

lore_entries.surface_form: Da Luo Jin Xian (大罗金仙)
lore_entries.description: A celestial cultivation level of extreme attainment; the minimum threshold required to even attempt to wield the Sword of Immortal Slaying without immediate death.

lore_entries.surface_form: Four Swords of Immortal Slaying (诛仙四剑)
lore_entries.description: The set of four primordial swords: Immortal Slaying, Immortal Execution, Immortal Extermination, and Immortal Annihilation. They function as a single weapon system with the formation diagram.
The sealed consciousness of an ancient creature captured and forced into the sword's core as its artifact spirit. It must be fed the wielder's blood regularly or it will attempt to devour its host.

faq_entries.question: Can the Sword of Immortal Slaying really kill immortals?
faq_entries.answer: The tradition says yes, but not through ordinary cutting. It severs the target's causal root—it erases them from the fabric of reality, making the destruction absolute.

faq_entries.question: What happens if someone tries to forge a similar sword today?
faq_entries.answer: The sword is a primordial treasure, not something that can be recreated. Attempting to replicate its principle would require capturing the slaughter law itself, which is beyond any modern cultivation.

faq_entries.question: Does the sword have any known counter?
faq_entries.answer: No independent weapon is specifically recorded as a counter. In the Fengshen narrative, the combined power of four Da Luo Jin Xian could disrupt the formation, but no single artifact is said to neutralize the blade.

faq_entries.question: Is the sword currently accessible to anyone?
faq_entries.answer: No. After Tongtian Jiaozhu's defeat, the sword was confiscated by the celestial authorities and sealed away—likely beyond the reach of the Three Realms.
